texts: good. the payment event carries all four participants — the village as payer, the Keepers as recipient, and food and shelter each as its own medium atom. Note that "the Keepers" is stored as a name-only label, so this sentence types nobody as a keeper.

mixed: "pools" names one act of combining three things, but a coordinated object list is replicated once per conjunct, so the parse gives three separate pooling events with no single pool tying them together — and nothing connects to "the pool" that the next sentence refers to. Rewrite as "The village puts its fishing harvest, grain trade, and garden produce into a common pool." — the three deposits then all share one pool symbol, which is the aggregation the original sentence means.

good. the explicit "each" gives a fireable per-Keeper rule with a share of its own drawn from the pool, at the right strength and confidence. Be aware that it only fires for individuals typed as keepers, and "the Keepers" in the first sentence is a name-only label that supplies no such typing.

bad: once the improvised trade event is removed — a bare oblique object like "for trade" has to stay a plain constant — "with outside merchants" has no slot left at all and the merchants vanish from the parse entirely; the extra "outside" property atom is unlicensed too. Rewrite as "The villagers use coin in order to trade with outside merchants." — the purpose infinitive reifies the trading as an event of its own, so the trading, the villagers who do it, and the outside merchants are all recorded and linked to the coin use.
